newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks reverse gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed earlier gains to close down for the first time since November 4, after dealers took profits on blue chips that had previously dragged the market up, traders said.
"Heavyweights like Telmex and Femsa hauled us up in the morning, and profit-takers stepped in later. After the recent run of gains, it had to happen," said a trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 8.74 points, or 0.26 percent, at 3,392.22. Volume as reasonable at 85.9 million shares traded.
On the broad market, 105 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 54 to 37.

Phone company Telmex L series ended up four centavos at 12.64 pesos, but off an early high of 12.80. Holding company Femsa ended down 30 centavos at 26.80 pesos, off a high of 27.25. Financial stock Serfin led the gainers, up 23 centavos at 3.70 pesos. Traders said this was a recovery after the markt had hit the stock hard recently, and noted it was well down from its year high of 6.24 pesos.
Another financial stocks, BBVPro, headed the losers, off four centavos at 41 centavos.

Several other financial stocks ended down, and traders noted that the banks' past-due loans problem was a cause for concern. Analysts noted that the IPC broke a psychological barrier at 3,400 points, but failed to reach a resistance at 3,440.
"We see 3,500 as being a short-term target, although some churning on the way would be natural," said Daniel Romo, research manager at the Bancrecer financial group.
Romo noted political controversy but said it was not hurting the bourse, referring to ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party deputies' reluctance to vote on a political reform bill before Congress.
"Dealers are beginning to digest the budget. This is a bull market, and we expect to see the year end at 3,700-3,750 points," Romo added.
